calls.note: P Sridhar of Kurnool asked for Kranthi by name about three holdings. Kranthi said the charts look fine and one can add on dips at these levels. In Fineotex there is speculative activity from time to time because investor Ashish Kacholia is in it - and he trimmed about 0.5% stake this quarter, booking some profit - but by and large the fundamentals are decent and they are talking of a next-two-years horizon, so one can add slowly.

Same call. Kranthi said Ather is now entering F&O and is an outperforming stock in the EV space, so Ather can be added on dips. The anchor confirmed the attribution: as Kranthi garu said, Ather Energy comes into F&O from August 26, along with Bank of Maharashtra and Sagility.

Same call. Kranthi said he has not tracked Hexagon and is not tracking it much - a recently listed company with nothing notable visible, some research-driven nutrition company. He said wait, give it some more time, and enter only after that.

Vaishali from Chennai asked which of Narayana Hrudayalaya and Acutaas Chemical is the better buy; the anchor asked Kranthi for his choice. Kranthi said if you want to be without risk you can add Narayana Hrudayalaya on dips - by and large the risk is very low and it is a business insulated from global crude oil prices. The whole healthcare sector has been in an uptrend since the day Trump announced tariffs and is still in an uptrend.

Same mail. Kranthi said if you have a risk appetite you can add Acutaas Chemical. But he cautioned that Acutaas has results today, so watch the results carefully and take the decision after seeing them.

Venkata Krishna Rao mailed asking whether to sell Infosys and buy Tech Mahindra or HCL Tech; the anchor asked Kranthi. He first said it depends upon risk appetite, then said Tech Mahindra's results are fine but Infosys is not to be ignored either - new management is coming and whether he takes the company on a different path has to be seen, because Infosys nearer to the 1,000 level is a very attractive buy for the long term. He called it a contrarian buy.
